rich_description: The Public Rental Scheme provides heavily subsidised 1-room and 2-room HDB rental flats for Singapore citizen families who genuinely cannot afford to buy a flat and have no other housing options. Rents start as low as $26 a month for the lowest income tier, scaling up to a few hundred dollars depending on household income. It is means-tested with a hard total household gross income ceiling of $1,500 a month, and applicants must show they have exhausted other avenues — no other property owned in the last 30 months, family unable or unwilling to house them, and no recent flat sale proceeds. The flat is rented, not owned: there is no resale value and tenancy is reviewed periodically. This is the housing scheme of last resort for the lowest-income citizens, including elderly singles, single parents, divorcees, and families who lost their previous flat. Waiting time can be long depending on flat type and location preferences; applicants in acute crisis (e.g. eviction from a private rental, homelessness) can ask their social worker to flag urgency through the Joint Singles Scheme or Interim Rental Housing pathways.

other_criteria: Singapore citizen applicant; occupiers can be citizen, PR, or non-citizen spouse
Total household gross income at or below $1,500 a month
No ownership of any private property or HDB flat in the last 30 months
Have no immediate family member who can adequately house the applicant
Singles must be 35 or older to apply on their own (under the Single Singapore Citizen Scheme or Joint Singles Scheme)

required_documents.name: Income documents
required_documents.notes: Payslips, CPF contribution history, or written income declaration; for unemployed members a no-income declaration

required_documents.name: Eviction notice or proof of housing crisis

oth_location: Level 3, HDB Tampines Branch (Customer Service Counters). Family Service Centre at OTH can assist with application preparation and write supporting letters for low-income families.
typical_processing_time: Initial eligibility assessment 4-6 weeks. Allocation of an actual flat depends on stock and family-size preferences — can range from a few months to over a year. Urgent cases routed through interim housing may be placed within weeks.
